documents.abstract: Background: Difficult airway management requires appropriate assessment, planning, technical skills, teamwork, and effective use of cognitive aids. Human factors may influence decision-making during challenging airway situations. This study explored the experiences of airway practitioners and identified facilitators and barriers in routine airway instrumentation using the SEIPS framework. Methods: A qualitative study using thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s approach was conducted at a tertiary care center in Kottayam, Kerala. Fifteen anaesthesiologists or emergency physicians with at least five years of airway-management experience were purposively selected. Data were collected through in-depth face-to-face interviews conducted between October 2024 and October 2025. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using an inductive approach, with themes and subthemes developed and reviewed by the investigators. Results: Three initial codes, five major themes, and 15 subthemes emerged from the interviews. The major themes were clinical and problem-solving skills, training and teamwork, overcoming challenges, the role of tools in clinical decision-making, and sources of error in clinical decisions. Participants emphasized appropriate airway assessment, timely decision-making, teamwork, supervision, access to advanced airway devices, updated knowledge, and effective communication. Uncertainty from previous experiences, overconfidence, cognitive overload, poor communication, and system-related constraints were identified as barriers. Conclusion: Standardization, updated knowledge, teamwork, leadership, effective communication, and appropriate cognitive aids may help address challenges in airway management and bridge gaps between policy and clinical practice.

Near-field perception is essential for the safe operation of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) in manufacturing environments. Conventional ranging sensors such as light detection and ranging (LiDAR) and ultrasonic devices provide broad situational awareness but often fail to detect small objects near the robot base. To address this limitation, this paper presents a three-tier near-field perception framework. The first approach employs light-discontinuity detection, which projects a laser stripe across the near-field zone and identifies interruptions in the stripe to perform fast, binary cutoff sensing for obstacle presence. The second approach utilizes light-displacement measurement to estimate object height by analyzing the geometric displacement of a projected stripe in the camera image, which provides quantitative obstacle height information with minimal computational overhead. The third approach employs a computer vision-based object detection model on embedded AI hardware to classify objects, enabling semantic perception and context-aware safety decisions. All methods are implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5 system, achieving real-time performance at 25 or 50 frames per second. Experimental results show that Approach 1 achieves a 99.0% average detection success rate across ten near-field object classes, Approach 2 achieves 2.4 mm RMSE in height estimation on representative samples, and Approach 3 achieves 100% mAP@0.5 on the held-out synthetic test set for ten-class object classification. Experimental evaluation and comparative analysis demonstrate that the proposed hierarchy balances precision, computation, and cost, thereby providing a scalable perception solution for enabling safe operations of AMRs in manufacturing environments.

Abstract India’s National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 articulates an ambitious vision for the comprehensive reform of higher education, foregrounding technology integration, multidisciplinary learning, and learner-centred pedagogy as central pillars. Concurrently, the global proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) across educational domains has prompted serious scholarly and policy-level engagement with its transformative potential and inherent risks. This paper presents a critical analysis of the intersection between NEP 2020 and AI-driven transformation in three core dimensions of higher education: teaching, learning, and assessment. Drawing upon verified policy documents, systematic reviews, and empirical studies published by reputable international bodies and journals between 2016 and 2025, the paper examines how NEP 2020’s policy architecture creates both affordances and constraints for AI adoption. The analysis reveals that while the policy’s emphasis on digital infrastructure, personalised learning, and continuous assessment aligns substantively with global AI-in-education trajectories, significant challenges persist regarding equitable access, faculty preparedness, ethical governance, and assessment integrity. The paper argues that realising NEP 2020’s AI-enabled vision demands a critical, context-sensitive implementation strategy that moves beyond techno-optimism toward principled, evidence-informed integration.

Fraud represents a growing and complex threat in contemporary societies, with consequences that extend beyond economic losses. Despite increasing international evidence, limited research has examined the psychological and cognitive factors associated with fraud victimization in the Italian context, particularly in relation to online scams. This study examines individual differences and fraud experiences among 600 Italian adults through an online survey assessing sociodemographic characteristics, fraud experiences, personality traits, gullibility, financial literacy, and financial self-efficacy. Results revealed that more than half of the sample ( n = 416) reported exposure to scam attempts, most of which occurred through remote channels (either exclusively online or in combination with offline channels). A smaller subset ( n = 115) reported actual fraud victimization. A binomial logistic regression was conducted to identify individual factors associated with fraud victimization among exposed individuals. Gullibility emerged as the only statistically significant predictor, indicating that higher gullibility was associated with a greater likelihood of victimization, whereas sociodemographic characteristics, personality traits, financial literacy, and financial self-efficacy were not significantly associated with victimization. These findings highlight that fraud prevention strategies may benefit from considering psycho-cognitive vulnerability factors alongside traditional financial and digital literacy initiatives.

Abstract Low lunar orbits that persist over a long duration without impacting the Moon continue to interest the astrodynamics community for trajectory design and space situational awareness. To support exploratory analysis of these low lunar, long-lifetime trajectories in a high-fidelity dynamical model, this paper uses a clustering-based approach. First, low lunar trajectories are numerically generated from coarsely sampled initial conditions for up to 180 days in a 100 $$\times $$ × 100 lunar gravity model along with the point mass gravity of the Earth and Sun. Each trajectory is represented by a subset of its perilunes in a Moon-fixed frame. Distributed trajectory clustering is then used to group trajectories with a similar evolution of eccentricity and argument of perilune, regardless of their initial phasing. From selected global clusters, trajectories with a low level of drift in their evolution of perilune over 180 days and geometrically distinct perilune groundtracks are isolated as long-lifetime orbits. Sets of geometrically similar long-lifetime orbits are presented, analyzed, and then coarsely compared to analytically derived frozen orbit predictions from the existing literature.

DESCRIPTION OBSERVE Protocol v1.0 — Version 7 defines a longitudinal research infrastructure for transforming institutional communications, responses, actions, permissions, public-record pathways, and digitally observable events into structured, verifiable, provenance-aware research evidence. Version 7 extends the methodological foundations established in Versions 1–6 by explicitly treating institutional communication as a research event that can be recorded, verified, preserved, compared, and connected to subsequent open research outputs. The framework does not treat institutional communication as a conclusion in itself. Acknowledgement, substantive review, permission, endorsement, public-record inclusion, policy adoption, and observable institutional change are maintained as distinct evidence categories. This distinction is essential for preventing overstatement while preserving the research value of institutional interactions. Version 7 incorporates a new phase of the longitudinal observation record involving institutional communication concerning AI accountability, software and agentic AI identity and authorization, Citizen Auditing, and research provenance. It documents how external research contributions can enter institutional communication channels, how acknowledgement and public-record pathways can be preserved as research events, and how such interactions may subsequently generate new open research outputs. A central example is the documented research interaction with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) / National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence (NCCoE) concerning software and agentic AI identity and authorization. The corresponding research record connects institutional AI-accountability work with the OBSERVE methodology, longitudinal institutional observation, research provenance, and open research. Version 7 also records a separate administrative communication concerning a Public-Interest Research Contribution: Citizen Auditing and AI Accountability. The communication established an administrative acknowledgement and a pathway for potential public sharing in future meeting minutes. The researcher's confirmation of permission is preserved as a provenance event. The framework does not interpret this acknowledgement or permission as substantive institutional review, endorsement, policy adoption, or validation of the underlying research. The same provenance principle is extended to communications with academic units concerning quotation, citation, attribution, and permission to reuse research material. Such communications are treated as research-provenance events because they document how research material moves between researchers, institutions, academic audiences, and subsequent publications. The methodological cycle remains: OBSERVE → RECORD → VERIFY → PRESERVE → COMPARE → RESPOND → LEARN Version 7 therefore expands the original observation model into the following research-evidence pathway: Institutional Communication → Observation → Evidence → Research Provenance → Open Research Output → Longitudinal Analysis → Learning The framework establishes explicit boundaries between: acknowledgement and substantive review; permission and endorsement; public-record pathways and confirmed publication; temporal sequence and causal evidence; institutional communication and institutional adoption; research dissemination and institutional validation. This bounded-inference approach enables institutional interactions to be studied without converting administrative communication into unsupported conclusions. Version 7 further connects OBSERVE with emerging AI Accountability Literacy, particularly the methodological questions of how AI actions can be identified, authenticated, authorized, observed, recorded, verified, and preserved as research evidence. The framework is designed for research involving digital platforms, public and private institutions, regulatory environments, AI systems, agentic AI, citizen auditing, institutional observation, research provenance, open science, and longitudinal accountability research. Its central methodological proposition is: When institutional accountability increasingly depends upon traceable evidence, the provenance, verification, preservation, and longitudinal comparability of institutional observation become part of the research infrastructure through which accountability can be studied. OBSERVE Protocol v1.0 — Version 7 is therefore not a legal framework, regulatory assessment, judicial determination, or institutional evaluation. It is a research and evidence infrastructure designed to make institutional observation reproducible, auditable, provenance-aware, and suitable for longitudinal research. Version 7 treats the research record as cumulative. Earlier observations are not overwritten by later developments. New institutional communications, responses, permissions, public records, publications, technical changes, non-responses, and other observable events are added as subsequent research events. The record remains open to verification, comparison, and learning. documents.abstract: Motorcycle riders face numerous occupational risks as a result of their exposure to road traffic accidents, environmental conditions, and ergonomic difficulties. This study looked at the use of personal protective equipment and occupational hazards by motorcycle riders in Rivers West Senatorial District, Rivers State. Five objectives, five research questions, and two hypotheses were developed and tested to a significance level of 0.05. With a population of 8,595 motorcyclists in Rivers West Senatorial District, Rivers State, and a sample size of 756 motorcyclists from Rivers West's various local governments, the study employed a descriptive cross-sectional survey design. The reliability coefficient of the self-structured questionnaire that was used for data collection was 0.91, and it was validated by three professors in the department of Human Kinetics, Health, and Safety Education. According to the study's findings, the result demonstrated that motorcyclists were particularly susceptible to physical danger (3.06 0.48). The findings of this study are to be expected because riders are exposed to numerous physically hazardous factors while riding. There was a negative correlation because when riders use personal protective devices like nose masks, eye goggles, and protective clothing, they are less likely to be exposed to physical hazards. When riders use PPD, they are more likely to be exposed to more hazards. It was recommended among others that management of road transport workers should put necessary laws to enforce the utilization of personal protective devices like eye goggle, nose masks, reflective and helmet by drivers or riders to reduce exposure to physical hazards and accidents among motorcyclists, the national union of road transport workers NURTW through their various bodies in rural and urban areas should establish regulatory personnel’s to ensure that there is strict compliance to safety by putting on the necessary protective devices by drivers/riders and fine should be paid for those that fail to comply.

documents.abstract: Solid waste scavenging provides livelihood for many in Nigeria but exposes scavengers to health hazards and chronic diseases. This study assessed solid waste scavenging and its potential health risks in Potiskum Metropolis, Yobe State. Using a descriptive survey design, 386 respondents were sampled from five wards. Data were collected through simple random and accidental sampling at dumpsites and analyzed using descriptive statistics. Findings revealed that most scavengers were male (97%), largely under 18 years (62%), and earned daily income above ₦950 (42%). Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) was low. Major health problems included infectious diseases, respiratory problems, injury, fatigue, and skin infections. Recommendations include PPE promotion, skill acquisition programs, formalization and monitoring of scavenging activities, and health awareness campaigns

documents.abstract: Automated ideation systems are often evaluated on the novelty of the ideas they produce, and that judgment is increasingly delegated to large language models. Such judges are typically built ad hoc and validated, if at all, on human-authored papers rather than on the generated ideas they are meant to score. So, how do novelty judges perform? Not well. We present a systematic controlled study of novelty evaluation design choices. We first build an evaluation set automatically, mining OpenReview for passages where reviewers explicitly affirm or dispute a paper's originality and keeping only submissions with unanimous agreement at the extremes of their research area; we pair these with ideas from a vanilla LLM generator. Across six judges, we find that small prompt design choices have large consequences; e.g., simply telling the judge that reviewers found one idea novel and the other not can change its verdict on more than half of the identical idea pairs it is shown, shifting pairwise accuracy by over 50 points and occasionally pushing it below chance. The same change helps one judge and hurts another. Retrieval and larger reasoning budgets help little, and two purpose-built novelty evaluators are outperformed by our cheapest prompted baseline. These results raise questions about reported novelty gains of automated ideation systems, and call for robust novelty evaluation methods.
